title: Create your Terms of Reference for a tailored ecosystem service assessment
completedHtml:
Thank you for your efforts!

A Terms of Reference has been automatically downloaded as a Word document for you to read and amend further. Check your downloads folder :)

back to home page

pages.name: page18
pages.title: A. Introduction
pages.description: Welcome to the creation of your Terms of Reference through an online survey! Depending on your case for an ecosystem service assessment, it can take you between 30 and 50 minutes to complete it. We will ask you some questions to automatically generate the Frame & Scope, and Methodology sections of a Terms of Reference based on your answers. The quality of your answers will determine the quality of the draft Terms of Reference that you will create. Also, while survey questions are in English, you can answer in any language. Some post processing using a translator may then be needed once your Terms of Reference is generated as it has been primarily designed for English language. Note: This survey does not cover the entirety of our writing guidance, see [Caveats and limitations](/caveats-limitations).

pages.name: page19
pages.title: B. Frame & Scope
pages.description: This section focuses on framing and scoping your ecosystem service assessment. It addresses: (1) the context and purpose of the assessment; (2) general characteristics such as the time period and geographical location; and (3) the involvement of stakeholders. Note: In our full writing guidance, this section also covers the intended impacts and the format of the outputs.

elements.name: fs_purpose_1a
elements.title: What is(are) the purpose(s) of the ecosystem service assessment? Is it part of a decision-making process? If so, at which step(s) of this process is the assessment needed?
elements.description: Identify the purpose of the assessment: what will the results of the assessment help you achieve? If part of a decision-making process, identify the step(s) for which you require this assessment: what will the results of this assessment help you achieve in terms of decision-making? Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_context_policy_1b
elements.title: Which relevant policies should be considered for the ecosystem service assessment given the decision-making step and primary objective?
elements.description: Identify the international and national policies that should be considered in the ecosystem service assessment. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_context_social_1d
elements.title: What is the social / demographic context of the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Identify the key social and demographic characteristics of the area and / or populations interacting with the ecosystems to be assessed. These characteristics may include age distribution, cultural and ethnic composition, income levels, education, livelihood types etc. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_context_decision_1e
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment aim at providing recommendations within the decision-making and policy context?
elements.description: Providing recommendations means identifying and describing actionable suggestions to improve or bridge an existing gap of a strategy or situation.

pages.name: page2
pages.title: B.2 Ecosystem type(s) and service(s) of interest

elements.name: fs_meth_es_31b
elements.title: What ecosystem service(s) is(are) of interest in the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Identify and define the ecosystem service(s) that should be focused on in the assessment. Ecosystem services are the contributions of ecosystems that support economic activities and other aspects of human well-being, such as urban cooling, flood protection, pollination, timber and food provision etc. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_meth_et_31a
elements.title: What ecosystem type(s) is(are) of interest in the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Identify and define the ecosystem type(s) that should be focused on in the assessment. Ecosystem types refer to different environments where living things interact with each other and their surroundings. Examples of ecosystem types include forests, city parks, wetlands, sand dunes etc. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_meth_sp_ext_32a
elements.title: What is(are) the geographical location(s) and total area(s) (i.e., spatial extent) of the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Identify the geographical location(s) and total area of each location (e.g., 5,000 m2, 1 km2, 10 ha) in which the assessment should be conducted. The geographical location and the total area form the spatial extent. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_meth_sp_scale_32b
elements.title: At which spatial scale(s) should the results of the ecosystem service assessment be presented (e.g., results aggregated to administrative scales such as regions and counties)?
elements.description: Select what applies. The spatial scales apply within the geographical location and spatial extent chosen of the ecosystem service assessment.

choices.text: Fully spatially explicit: the assessment maps detailed spatial patterns and interactions to support site-specific management.
Aggregation at ecological scale: the assessment aggregates ecosystem types and services by groups that are ecologically meaningful.
Aggregation at administrative scale: the assessment averages ecosystem service results by administrative areas.

elements.name: fs_meth_sp_agg_ecolo
elements.title: You indicated that the results should be aggregated at ecological scales. Please specify the ecological groups that are meaningful to the assessment. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_meth_sp_agg_admin
elements.title: You indicated that the results should be aggregated at administrative scales. Please specify the administrative groups that are meaningful to the assessment. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: fs_meth_temp_33a
elements.title: What is the time period and temporal scale(s) to be considered in the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Identify the total time period (or interval) for which the ecosystem service assessment is to be conducted. It may also be a single (e.g., annual) assessment without repetition. Then specify the temporal scale, in which you need the results reported. The temporal scale represents the unit of time in which the results should be presented (aggregated if needed) such as by year, by quarter, by month, etc. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

items.name: time_scale
items.title: Temporal scale (results reported by year, quarter, month…)

elements.name: fs_meth_biophy_34a
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service(s) be measured in biophysical terms?
elements.description: Valuing, or quantifying, ecosystem services in biophysical terms means that the assessment measures the physical quantity of the ecosystem service (e.g., tonnes of crops produced, tonnes of carbon sequestrated, number of recreational visitors).

elements.name: fs_meth_biophy_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Measuring ecosystem services in biophysical terms is at the foundation of all other measures of ecosystems services such as economic valuation, or health and social benefits of these services. Do you confirm that you do not wish any biophysical measure of ecosystems services?

elements.name: fs_meth_econo_34b
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service(s) be measured in terms of their economic value in monetary units?
elements.description: Economic value is a measure of the contribution of the ecosystem service(s) to human wellbeing. It is generally measured in monetary units to facilitate direct comparison and aggregation with the values of other goods and services (e.g., for inclusion in decision support frameworks such as cost-benefit analysis). It is recommended to first value service in biophysical terms before valuing them in monetary terms.

elements.name: fs_meth_econo_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Your answer to this question means that we will not ask you any further question on economic valuation. Your Terms of Reference will then not include any sections on economic valuation of ecosystem services. Do you confirm this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: fs_meth_es_measure_34c
elements.title: What aspects of ecosystem services should be measured?
elements.description: Select what applies.

rows.text: Ecosystem service supply: quantity of ecosystem service being supplied.
Ecosystem service use: quantity of ecosystem service being used.
Ecosystem service demand: quantity of ecosystem service being needed.

elements.name: fs_meth_es_confirmation
elements.title: Your answer to this question means that the contractor will not know what aspect of ecosystem service(s) to measure. Think about your context and purpose and select the feature that would be the most relevant to you. If you are sure of your answers or still don’t know, please select one of the answers below.

choices.text: I am sure of my answers

elements.name: fs_meth_sust_34f
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment evaluate the conservation, sustainable supply and / or use of the ecosystem service(s) of interest?
elements.description: Sustainable use of ecosystem services means that the services will be maintained and won’t be used until depletion, but will be available for future generations. Sustainable supply of ecosystem services means that they will continue to be provided in the long term and be available for future generations. The assessment of sustainable levels of supply and use facilitates the evaluation of sustainability of use, management and conservation measures.

elements.name: fs_meth_sust_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Your answer to this question means that we will not ask you any further questions on ecosystem services conservation and sustainability. Your Terms of Reference will then not include any sections on ecosystem services conservation and sustainability. Do you confirm this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: fs_meth_social_34d
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment address social benefits and equity goals?
elements.description: Social benefits are improvements in people’s quality of life. Equity goals focus on guaranteeing that these are fairly distributed among social groups. Social benefit is a measure of the contribution of ecosystem services to societal well-being and equity. It can be quantified using metrics such as availability and access to ecosystem services, reduction in social vulnerabilities, social inclusion, etc.

elements.name: fs_meth_social_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Your answer to this question means that we will not ask you any further questions on social benefits and equity goals. Your Terms of Reference will then not include any sections on social benefits and equity goals. Do you confirm this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: fs_meth_health_34e_1
elements.title: Should the ecosystem services be valued in terms of their relevance to health?
elements.description: Ecosystem services are crucial to health, including the health dimension in an ecosystem service assessment allows to take into account the wider impacts of changes in ecosystem services on the society and the environment. The health scope will inform the selection of assessment methodology, stakeholder engagement and reporting.

elements.name: fs_meth_health_34e
elements.title: Should the assessment look at human, animal, or plant health, or take a One Health approach combining all three with ecosystem health?
elements.description: The One Health approach is an approach that recognises the interconnection between people, animals, plants and their shared environment.

rows.text: One health: recognises the interconnection between people, animals, plants and their shared environment

elements.name: fs_meth_health_confirmation
elements.visibleIf:
({fs_meth_health_34e_1} anyof ['no', 'dontknow']) or ({fs_meth_health_34e.human_health} anyof ['no','dontknow'] and
{fs_meth_health_34e.animal_health} anyof ['no','dontknow'] and
{fs_meth_health_34e.plant_health} anyof ['no','dontknow'] and
{fs_meth_health_34e.one_health} anyof ['no','dontknow'])
elements.title: Note: Your answer to this question means that we will not ask you any further questions on health. Your Terms of Reference will then not include any sections on health. Do you confirm this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: fs_meth_cond_34g
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment include an evaluation of ecosystem condition?
elements.description:
Ecosystem condition characterises the state of health of ecosystems. Ecosystem services are sensitive to a change in condition of the ecosystem that provides the service. Ecosystems in bad condition might have less capacity to provide 
ecosystem services.

elements.name: fs_meth_cond_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Your answer to the previous question means that we will not ask you any further questions on ecosystem condition. Your Terms of Reference will then not include any sections on the ecological condition of ecosystems. Do you confirm this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: fs_meth_scenario_35a
elements.title: Are future scenarios required in the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Identify if there is a need to conduct the assessment while taking into account scenarios reflecting a change in policy, climate or other environmental conditions, change in governance etc. In modelling, future scenarios represent a range of potential futures that one would like to predict.

elements.name: fs_meth_scenario_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Your answer to this question means that we will not ask you any further questions on future scenarios. Your Terms of Reference will then not include any sections on futures scenarios. Do you confirm this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: fs_stake_analysis_4a
elements.title: Should the contractor conduct a stakeholder analysis?
elements.description: A stakeholder analysis aims at identifying and understanding third parties (i.e., individuals, groups, organisations/institutions) who are interested in or are expected to have an impact on the process of the ecosystem service assessment and / or its results.

elements.name: fs_stake_involv_4b
elements.title: Is it anticipated that any stakeholder(s) will be involved at any stage of the ecosystem assessment process (e.g., assessment development, practice, review, reporting)?
elements.description: Stakeholder engagement means that key parties will be consulted during the development of the assessment and the evaluation of the results and deliverables.

elements.name: fs_meth_stakeholder_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Your answer to this question means that we will not ask you any further questions on stakeholder engagement. Your Terms of Reference will then not include any sections on stakeholder engagement. Do you confirm this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: fs_stake_id_4c
elements.title: If key stakeholders have already been identified for direct involvement in the ecosystem service assessment: who are they and why have they been selected?
elements.description: Identify the stakeholders who should be consulted during the development of the assessment. This can be based on an earlier stakeholder analysis or primary considerations that are important from the commissioners’ perspective.

pages.name: page20
pages.title: C. Methodology
pages.description: This section focuses on the methodology of your ecosystem service assessment. It identifies the methodological features of your ecosystem service assessment based on your selection of topics in the Frame & Scope section.

elements.name: me_expertise_needed_1
elements.title: Do you have the expertise to choose the economic valuation methods you would like to be applied in your assessment?

elements.name: me_econ_valuation_11a
elements.title: Which economic valuation method(s) should be applied in the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Select what applies. Value transfer methods use existing study results to estimate values for new sites, usually faster and cheaper alternative to primary valuation. Primary valuation methods produce new or original information generally using primary data for the specific location of the assessment.

elements.name: me_econ_valuation_condition
elements.title: You answered “No” to both methods proposed above. Please specify the methods you would like to recommend for you assessment.
elements.description: Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: me_primary_valuation_condition
elements.title: You selected that primary valuation methods should be applied, do you wish to specify which primary valuation methods?

elements.name: me_valuation_methods
elements.title: Please select the primary valuation method(s) that you want to be applied from the list below

elements.name: other_valuation
elements.title: You selected 'Other', please specify the economic valuation method(s) that are of interest in the assessment:
elements.description: Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: me_econ_dev_11b
elements.title: Should the assessment include indicators of the contribution of ecosystem service(s) to economic development such as employment and growth?
elements.description: If yes and if commissioners have the knowledge, they can specify the type of economic indicator of interest. The economic importance of ecosystem services can be quantified through indicators such as the contribution to economic development, sectors of the economy, or employment. These indicators can be useful for communicating the importance of ecosystem services to decision makers and the general public.

elements.name: me_econo_id
elements.title: Please specify the economic indicator(s) that are of interest in the assessment:
elements.description: Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: me_eco_con_12a
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment evaluate how the condition of ecosystems influences the levels of ecosystem services supply and use?
elements.description: Ecosystem condition relates to the quality of an ecosystem. The levels of ecosystem service(s) supply and use may vary depending on changes in condition of the ecosystem that provides the service. Ecosystem service(s) supply is the provision of service(s) by the ecosystem(s). Ecosystem service(s) use is the utilisation of service(s) by those who benefit from them.

elements.name: me_sust_level_12b
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment evaluate and define sustainable levels for the use and / or supply of ecosystem services?
elements.description: Sustainable use of ecosystem services means that the ecosystem services won’t be used until depletion and will still be available for future generations. Sustainable supply of ecosystem services means that they will continue to be provided long-term and be available for future generations. Defining sustainable levels refers to the evaluation and identification of maximum use that is compatible with the supply of ecosystem services. If these levels are respected, the ecosystem condition and ability to deliver services for future generations is maintained.

elements.name: me_expertise_needed
elements.title: Do you have the expertise to choose the condition indicators you would like to be applied in your assessment?

elements.name: me_ecos_cond_12c
elements.title: What aspects of ecosystem condition are you interested in?
elements.description: Ecosystem condition encompasses a lot of different dimensions. Select those of interest in this assessment.

rows.text: Index of general ecosystem condition: overarching measure of ecosystem condition combining several condition indicators.
Biotic indicators – species: show how well species are doing in an ecosystem
Biotic indicators – structure: show how well the physical structure of an ecosystem is doing
Biotic indicators – function: inform about the level of specific ecological functions and processes of an ecosystem
Abiotic - physical indicators: show levels of non-living physical components of an ecosystem (e.g., soil pH, water temperature)
Abiotic - chemical indicators: show the chemical properties in water, soil and air of an ecosystem
Landscape-level characteristics: assess how an ecosystem is physically organised in space.

elements.name: me_soc_groups_13a
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment results be disaggregated by social groups to better understand who benefits from ecosystem services?
elements.description: Understanding who benefits from the ecosystem services guarantees that inequities are identified and addressed. This approach highlights who benefits, who is excluded, and how interventions can improve well-being and equity. Examples of social groups are: gender, age, race, ethnicity, (dis)ability, income status, etc.

elements.name: me_soc_groups_13b
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment evaluate and report the attitudes, perceptions, and values of social groups towards ecosystem services?
elements.description: This allows to investigate whether the ecosystem service assessment will document how different social groups perceive, value, and prioritize ecosystem services.

pages.name: page11
pages.visibleIf: {fs_meth_health_34e.human_health} anyof ['yes','maybe'] or {fs_meth_health_34e.animal_health} anyof ['yes','maybe'] or {fs_meth_health_34e.plant_health} anyof ['yes','maybe'] or {fs_meth_health_34e.one_health} anyof ['yes','maybe'] or {fs_meth_health_confirmation} = 'no'
pages.title: C.4 Health characteristics

elements.name: me_health_aspects_14a
elements.title: What aspects of health are you interested in?
elements.description: Select what applies.

rows.text: Health benefits: include goods or services promoting good health or offer avenues for positive health interventions.
Health risks: potential threats to good health, including drivers of disease emergence.
Health outcomes: status of health as a result of an intervention or exposure to one or more conditions.

elements.name: me_health_social_14b
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment evaluate and report the attitudes, perceptions, and values of social groups towards health-relevant ecosystem services?
elements.description: Investigate whether the ecosystem service assessment will document how different social groups perceive, value, and prioritize ecosystem services. These perceptions may include cultural significance, recreational use, or economic reliance.

elements.name: me_health_eco_14c
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment establish health links with specific ecosystem types and / or ecosystem services?
elements.description: This determines whether the ecosystem service assessment will consider general relationships between environmental compartments (e.g. air, water, soil, urban environments, rural landscapes etc.) and health, or aim to provide a more detailed understanding of the impact of defined ecosystems types and / or their services on specific health issues.

elements.name: me_eco_relations_15a
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment identify potential interrelationships between ecosystem services and / or the benefits they provide?
elements.description: Interrelationships between ecosystem services, between benefits, or between ecosystem services and their benefits means that the services and / or benefits are related and affect each other. There are a number of ways ecosystems services and / or benefits can be related such as interdependencies, synergies, and trade-offs.

elements.name: me_eco_relations_15b
elements.title: Which interrelationship(s) is(are) of interest in this assessment?

rows.text: Interrelationships between ecosystem services and their benefits

elements.name: me_spatial_benefits_16a
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment evaluate how the distribution of ecosystem service(s) and the benefits they provide vary across the space?
elements.description: This helps determine whether the assessment should quantify and track how the ecosystem service supply, use, demand but also the benefits derived from them vary across the geographic areas and spatial scales (e.g., continental, national, regional, local) considered in the assessment. For example, this could allow to identify differences in supply and / or benefits between different countries, regions, municipalities, or other relevant areas.

elements.name: me_time_benefits_16b
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment evaluate how the distribution of ecosystem service(s) and the benefits they provide change over time?
elements.description: This allows for quantifying and tracking how the ecosystem service(s) supply, use, demand but also the benefits derived from them vary over time due to management actions, environmental factors, or policy changes.

elements.name: me_time_space_sustainability_16c
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assessment put the spatial / temporal variations of ecosystem services in relation with the sustainable use / supply?
elements.description: This allows to reveal trends in supply and use over time and geographic areas to highlight critical mismatches between the actual levels of use and supply and the levels of use and supply that are considered as sustainable. This is important in prioritising interventions that prevent depletion and ensure long-term supply and use of the services.

elements.name: me_time_space_condition_16d
elements.visibleIf: {me_sust_level_12b} anyof ['yes', 'maybe'] and ({fs_meth_cond_34g} anyof ['yes','maybe'] or {fs_meth_cond_confirmation} = 'no') and ({me_spatial_benefits_16a.space_es} anyof ['yes','maybe'] or {me_time_benefits_16b.time_es} anyof ['yes','maybe'])
elements.title: Should the ecosystem service assesment provide recommendations for maintaining or enhancing the supply / use of the ecosystem services without negatively affecting the ecosystem condition
elements.description: Providing recommendations means identifying and describing actionable suggestions to improve or bridge an existing gap of a strategy or situation.

elements.name: me_scenarios_17a
elements.title: What scenarios should be taken into account in the ecosystem service assessments?
elements.description:
List and describe the scenarios that should be taken into account, for example scenario description 1, scenario description 2, etc. If you are unsure, leave the answer blank. Even a broad description of goals for which the scenarios are required is sufficient. In modelling, future scenarios represent a range of potential futures that one would like to predict. 
Skip this question if you really don't know.

elements.name: me_uncertainties_2a
elements.title: Should the uncertainties inherent to the ecosystem service assessment be assessed and documented for the purpose of the decision-making?
elements.description: Uncertainty is present in all ecosystem service assessments. It is essential that both the commissioners and potential contractors are conscious of the sources of uncertainty that matter for a particular purpose. We recommend that commissioners ask for the assessment and documentation of uncertainties pertaining to any results of their requested assessment.

elements.name: me_uncertainty_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Informed decision-making needs to take into account these uncertainties as they pertain to the robustness, relevance, and reliability of the results upon which they rely. Your answer to this question means that the results of the ecosystem service assessment will be presented without any indication on the degree of confidence. The section will thus be absent from your Terms of Reference. Do you confirm that this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: me_uncertainties_2b
elements.title: What is the preferred reporting format to document uncertainties?
elements.description: Select what applies.

rows.text: Uncertainty section/report: separate uncertainty section of the main report or a separate short deliverable
Visual summary: visuals showing results reliability (e.g., green-orange-red system)
Decision-relevant summary: designed for decision-making and can take different forms
Participatory documentation: qualitative approach relying on expert and stakeholder judgments

elements.name: me_uncertainties_2b_dup
elements.title: What is the preferred reporting format to document uncertainties?
elements.description: Select what applies.

rows.text: Uncertainty section/report: separate uncertainty section of the main report or a separate short deliverable
Visual summary: visuals showing results reliability (e.g., green-orange-red system)
Decision-relevant summary: designed for decision-making and can take different forms
Scenario-based documentation: relevant only if a scenario analysis is requested
Participatory documentation: qualitative approach relying on expert and stakeholder judgments

elements.name: me_uncertainties_2b_other
elements.title: You selected “Other”. Please specify the reporting of uncertainties that should be applied in the assessment. Note: Your draft Terms of Reference will display your answer as written here.

elements.name: me_validation_3a
elements.title: How should the methodology and results of the ecosystem service assessment be validated?
elements.description: Select what applies. Validating the methodology means ensuring that the metrics, data, choice of scenarios and analyses, and stakeholder involvement plan chosen meet the goals of the commissioners. Validating the results of the assessment means verifying that the findings are accurate, reliable, and answer the goals of the commissioners.

elements.name: me_validation_3b
elements.title: Should the results be compared to other published reference data in the validation process?
elements.description: Reference data are baseline or benchmark datasets or already published figures that will be used to compare the results of the ecosystem service assessment. Commissioners might want to list some key datasets or figures they would like the results to be comparable with. Alternatively, stakeholders can be consulted to identify these references.

elements.name: me_validation_3b_confirmation
elements.title: Note: Validation of the results gives an estimation of their quality. Your answer to this question means that the results of the ecosystem service assessment will not be validated. The section will thus be absent from your Terms of Reference. Do you confirm that this corresponds to your needs?

elements.name: me_stakeholder_engage_4a
elements.title: At which step(s) of the ecosystem service assessment should the stakeholders be informed, consulted, or participate?
elements.description:
Select what applies.
Identify when the stakeholders should be informed, consulted or participate in the ecosystem service assessment. Stakeholders are any group, organisation or individual who are interested in and / or might be affected by ecosystem services and any change made to their flows. In the context of an ecosystem service assessment, stakeholders notably include those who directly or indirectly benefit from the service, those who try to regulate the use, the experts in the science of ecosystem services, or the data holders.

rows.text: Validation of the methodology (e.g., metrics, indicators, data, choice of scenarios and analyses)
Communication and dissemination of the results

elements.name: me_stakeholder_engage_4a_other
elements.title: You selected “Other”. Please specify when the stakeholders should be involved in the assessment.

elements.name: me_stakeholder_engage_4b
elements.title: What methods should be used for involving stakeholders in the ecosystem service assessment?
elements.description: Describe how the stakeholders should be involved. Stakeholders are any group, organisation or individual who are interested in and / or will or might be affected by ecosystem services and any change made to their flows. In the context of an ecosystem service assessment, stakeholders notably include those who directly or indirectly benefit from the service, those who try to regulate the use, the experts in the science of ecosystem services, or the data holders. For this, the commissioner can choose from the table below:

rows.text: Advisory boards, expert groups, focus groups, or steering committees

elements.name: me_stakeholder_engage_4b_other
elements.title: You selected “Other”. Please specify how the stakeholders should be involved.

pages.name: page_end
pages.title: D. Survey Preview
pages.description: Well done! You finally made it to the end of the Terms of Reference survey! We will now show you a preview of your answers so you can check them and amend them if needed. Once you are done, click on Complete. This will generate your draft Terms of Reference as a Word document.
